chapter: Band family, war years and wrap-up
title: The recording ban and Petrillo
summary: He was told not to record and waited for the union.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Yeah. Now, another significant thing that happened during the war years was the ban on records that they had, you know, partly because they couldn't, they would make an agreement with record companies and also because they were saving the shellac. You know, so they had this record, recording ban there. Did that affect you? Did you feel that?

Right because we couldn't record no more. I remember Patrilla, one wire that they had out when recording was getting ready to start again. So, Patrilla sent everybody a wire to come to his office. I know I had to go to his office. And, when I walked
through that door he said, If you do it, I'll throw you out of the union for the rest of your life."

Now, I don't know what it was all about. I think I was in the Apollo Theater at the time. I went down there between shows. Then he told me. He started laughing. I said "What do you want?" He said, Didn't you get a wire from RCA Victor that everything had been settled?" I said yeah. He said well, "It hasn't been settled."

So, we had to stay off until everything was straight. Oh, that's right. Harry James was sitting out there to follow me in. He sent for everybody. Harry James was right behind me. He said how does it feel in there? I said he's pretty hot. And, I said just go and take it easy. He's not gonna bother you. I explained to him.
Yeah, he was something. But, that's about the only big thing during that time cause we just couldn't go back to recording until I got the word from him, until he sent us all
another wire cause they had mostly singing on records. Right?
Without instruments to back them up, choirs and all that.
